title: Discounted cash flows and model assumptions

objectives.text: Compute discount factors under explicit annual periodic versus continuous conventions,matching rate/time units and validating domains including zero time and negative rates.
Separate correct present-value arithmetic from the choice of curve,currency,credit/collateral,day count and promised-versus-uncertain cash-flow assumptions.
Distinguish interest from balance and follow the corrected repeated-multiplication balance-gap contract.

blocks.markdown: A present value translates a specified future cash amount into a value at an earlier valuation time under a stated model. For deterministic cash flow C at year fraction t,PV=C*D(0,t),where D is the matching discount factor. Amount and result must have the same currency;the factor is dimensionless. For several deterministic dated flows,PV=sum(C_i*D(0,t_i)). Each maturity can have its own factor. Negative cash flows are liabilities/outflows,not invalid merely because they are negative. These equations do not establish whether a promised payment will actually occur.

Write the rate convention before substituting a number. For annual effective rate r, D=(1+r)^(-t). For annual NOMINAL rate r compounded m times per year,D=(1+r/m)^(-m*t). For continuously compounded annual r,D=exp(-r*t). Here t is an already supplied year fraction,not a calendar date or a count of raw days. Domain1+r/m>0is needed for the real periodic formula. A rate5%means0.05,not5. These are own deterministic conventions;actual instruments also specify accrual,calendar and cash-flow timing rules.

blocks.title: The same quoted number is not the same rate contract

steps.text: Future110 after1year,annual effective10%:D=1/1.1,PV=100. Under continuous10%,D=exp(-0.1),so PV is about99.532116,not100.
To represent the SAME one-year growth1.1 continuously,use r_c=ln(1.1),not0.1. Then exp(-r_c)=1/1.1. More generally r_c=m*ln(1+r_nominal/m). Convert conventions before comparing yields.

At t=0,D=1. With negative continuous rate-5%for1year,D=exp(0.05)>1;discounting need not reduce a positive cash flow when rates are negative. Do not clamp a valid factor to1 because its direction looks unfamiliar.

blocks.markdown: Two promised flows110 at1year and121 at2years,discounted with flat annual effective10%,have PV100+100=200. A real term structure would supply D(0,1)and D(0,2)individually;using one flat yield is an assumption. Coupon-bond yield to maturity is the single internal rate reproducing that bond price from its whole promised schedule under its quotation convention. It is not automatically the correct spot rate for every separate maturity or every other product. Reconcile dates,amounts,currency,accrual fractions and instrument terms before computing.

A numerically correct factor can price the wrong claim if the curve does not match its currency,valuation date,collateral/funding,credit and instrument context. Government,overnight-indexed and unsecured issuer curves need not match. The Bank of England explicitly describes its yields as annual continuously compounded and distinguishes these curves from other frameworks. Do not treat a quoted UK curve as an automatically suitable curve for another currency or a risky corporate cash flow. Its historical LIBOR-related discussion is historical;those discontinued curves are not a current borrowing recommendation.

Discounting a promised amount as if it were certain is not the same as valuing defaultable or contingent cash flows. Expected real-world payoff discounted at an arbitrary risk-free rate is generally not a complete pricing argument. A model may need state-dependent payoffs,default/recovery,risk premia or a replication/risk-neutral framework. The next lesson derives a narrow two-state pricing weight;it is not a forecast of market returns. Keep calibrated inputs,as-of availability,units and assumptions with the result. A precise decimal does not certify that model assumptions fit the claim.

The example computes a factor only. Input validation rejects bools,integers at this exact-float boundary,NaN,infinity,unsupported convention and out-of-range values. That is an own pedagogic interface,not a statement that all finance APIs reject integer inputs. Bounded exponent ranges keep results finite here. Do not round each intermediate factor to two decimal places;retain precision and round the final display under an explicit currency/contract rule. Floating output is approximate,so independent tests compare tolerances against a higher-precision reference,not universal bitwise equality.

Sources:[Bank of England yield convention FAQ](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/statistics/yield-curves),[spot/forward/YTM definitions and curve caveats](https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/statistics/yield-curves/terminology-and-concepts),[CME model/carry/currency distinctions](https://cmegroupclientsite.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/pubsub/pages/457083416/SPAN+Risk+Manager+-+Option+Pricing+Models). Concrete bounds and flat-rate examples are own teaching choices,not current market quotes or investment advice.

Compare two balances, not balance against interest

After tyears at annual percentage r, simple balance is P*(1+r*t/100), compound balance is P*(1+r/100)^t. Their difference is interest-on-interest. The principal must appear in BOTH balances. Subtracting only P*r*t/100 from the compound balance leaves an extra P and was an earlier source defect, now corrected in the public contract and expected outputs.

Follow the requested operation order

The task specifically requires ordinary double parsing of the rate string and repeated multiplication: start compound=P, compute factor=1+r/100, and multiply by factor exactly t times. Do not replace the loop with pow/log despite the real-arithmetic identity, because rounding paths can differ. Compute simple=P*(1+r*t/100), then format abs(compound-simple) to two decimals. The original rate token remains a string argument; float(rate) is the explicit conversion prescribed by this public statement.

Trace, bounds and meaning

P1000,r5.00,t10 gives 128.89, not1128.89. P5000,r10.00,t3 gives 155.00. At t=1 the mathematical balance gap is 0; do not add principal a second time. Bounds t<=30,P<=1000000,r<=15 and a stated distance from cent ties make this a small bounded calculation, not a numerically arbitrary cash-flow engine. Compare against a high-precision rational/Decimal balance derivation and separately inspect the exact requested float loop. This is not a promised account rate or investment return.

blocks.source:
from collections import OrderedDict, deque
from bisect import bisect_left
import heapq
import math

def growth_gap(p, rate, t):
    annual_percent = float(rate)
    factor = 1 + annual_percent / 100
    compound = float(p)
    for _ in range(t):
        compound *= factor
    simple = p * (1 + annual_percent * t / 100)
    return [f'{abs(compound - simple):.2f}']

print(*growth_gap(1000, '5.00', 10))
print(*growth_gap(5000, '10.00', 3))

summary: Present-value arithmetic requires explicit rate compounding,time units and cash-flow dates. Match curve and claim assumptions separately;negative rates can imply factors above1,and a correct formula does not establish promised cash-flow certainty or an appropriate pricing model.
